events.did: was drowning under the lake ice, found the surface sealed into a solid ceiling and pounded on its underside
events.quote_anchor: By the time her fingers met the surface, it was a solid ceiling, and instead of bursting up, and through, and out, her palms found only smooth, unbroken ice.

events.did: cracked the ice beneath his palm and hauled Sydney out of the water
events.quote_anchor: The ice cracked beneath their palm, splintered, broke, and then their hand was wrapping around hers, fingers tangled as they hauled her up, out of the water.

events.did: woke drugged in a green-walled room at EON, curled in a chair with cotton in her head and sand-and-honey in her mouth
events.quote_anchor: She was curled in a chair, and her head felt full of cotton. A strange taste filled her mouth. Like sand and honey. Gritty, sweet.

events.did: sat down with Sydney at EON 30 minutes before the end and gave his name as Dr. Gray, telling her she could call him Gabriel
events.quote_anchor: He smiled, a shallow, automatic gesture. “My name is Dr. Gray,” he said, and she felt a small pang of vindication. “But you can call me Gabriel.”

events.did: had Eli brought in and told him he had been too rough with Sydney, making him apologize
events.quote_anchor: The Eli Ever Sydney knew would rather cut out his own heart. But this one looked flatly at her and said, with the hollowness of a recital, “I’m sorry.”

events.did: crushed the glass in her hand on Dr. Gray’s command, shattering it and cutting her hand on the shards
events.quote_anchor: The woman’s fingers vised, sudden and hard. The glass cracked, then shattered, collapsing inward. Jagged shards bit deep into her hand

events.did: made Helena collapse inward and disintegrate into ash
events.quote_anchor: And the next, she was gone, her body collapsing inward, the way the glass had done, skin and bone disintegrating into ash.

events.did: told Sydney that bringing Serena back was a mistake she needs to rectify, and Sydney asked if he wants her to kill her sister
events.quote_anchor: She stiffened. “What? How?” His gaze dropped to the ashes on the floor, and she almost laughed. “You want me to kill my sister?”

relations.did: is himself an EO whose power is like Sydney’s, and told her he brought Eli back
relations.quote_anchor: Sydney stiffened at this revelation. Not only that he was an EO, but that his power was like hers.

relations.did: was the director at EON before Dr. Gray arrived and is the one who hired him, but by now serves very little purpose
relations.quote_anchor: “Ms. Roy was the director here at EON, prior to my arrival,” he said, addressing Sydney. “In fact, she’s the one who hired me.”

relations.did: lacks independence: she keeps her knowledge and memory but has no agency and does exactly what Dr. Gray tells her to do
relations.quote_anchor: Ms. Roy, like all the humans I bring back, lacks a certain … independence. She retains her knowledge, and her memory, can access both as needed

relations.did: is Sydney’s sister and helped Eli find Sydney, knowing what he would do to her
relations.quote_anchor: She’s how Eli found me. She helped him, knowing what he’d do.

numbers.did: twice — the hand of the figure kneeling on the ice was twice the size of Sydney’s
numbers.quote_anchor: The figure knelt, fingers splayed, their hand twice the size of hers.

numbers.did: the first — Sydney was the first opportunity to investigate the similarities and differences between their powers
numbers.quote_anchor: “You present an opportunity—the first—to investigate the similarities, and differences.

numbers.did: the first time — bringing someone back is not hard if they just died, are still whole, and it is the first time
numbers.quote_anchor: “Not if they just died. And they’re still whole. And it’s the first time.

numbers.did: second — the second half of his twofold point, to show Sydney what else he can do
numbers.quote_anchor: And second…” He rested his hand on Helena Roy’s shoulder. “To show you what else I can do.”

numbers.did: more than once — she confirmed by bobbing her head that she can bring people back more than once
numbers.quote_anchor: “You can do it more than once?” interjected Dr. Gray. Sydney bobbed her head.

numbers.did: million-dollar — the question of why Serena helped Eli was the million-dollar question that had plagued her for years
numbers.quote_anchor: That was the million-dollar question. The one that had plagued Sydney all these years.
